title: Correlation Immunity of a Constant-Pair Function
statement: For every natural number $n$, define a function on the binary cube to equal $1$ at the zero vector and the all-ones vector, and $0$ elsewhere; convert its outputs to signs using $b\mapsto(-1)^b$ and identify the binary cube with the sign cube coordinatewise. The resulting sign-valued function is correlation immune of order $1$: every nonempty Fourier coefficient indexed by a set of at most one coordinate vanishes.
hypotheses_covered: The binary function is the indicator of the zero and all-ones vectors
